mechanics::kinematics in 1d/2d/3d.name: Timing and Displacement Relations
mechanics::kinematics in 1d/2d/3d.description: Kinematics tasks centered on time intervals, displacement symmetry, average speed, and one-dimensional motion relations.

rule_groups.name: Timing and Displacement Checks
rule_groups.summary: Checks time-interval, displacement, and average-speed reasoning in elementary kinematics.
rule_groups.activation_condition: Use when the core step is relating time, displacement, symmetry, or average speed.

mechanics::kinematics in 1d/2d/3d.name: Trajectory Geometry and Projection
mechanics::kinematics in 1d/2d/3d.description: Kinematic reasoning that uses geometric unfolding, collision sequences, or projected velocity/angle relations.

rule_groups.name: Trajectory and Projection Checks
rule_groups.summary: Checks geometry-heavy kinematics where trajectories are unfolded, projected, or constrained by impact order.
rule_groups.activation_condition: Use when trajectory geometry, reflections, or projection relations dominate the setup.

mechanics::kinematics in 1d/2d/3d.name: Constraint-Based Kinematics
mechanics::kinematics in 1d/2d/3d.description: Kinematics under geometric or mechanical constraints, including lateral acceleration and coupled-motion consistency.

rule_groups.name: Constraint Motion Checks
rule_groups.summary: Checks whether constrained-motion kinematics are built with the correct relation between geometry and acceleration.
rule_groups.activation_condition: Use when the motion is constrained by geometry or linkage rather than free evolution.

mechanics::newton's laws and free body d.name: Drag and Equation Setup
mechanics::newton's laws and free body d.description: Free-body modeling where drag form, parameter normalization, and equation setup are the main source of mistakes.

rule_groups.name: Drag and Setup Checks
rule_groups.summary: Checks whether Newtonian equations are set up with the correct force form and simplification regime.
rule_groups.activation_condition: Use when the challenge is choosing or simplifying the force equation itself.

mechanics::friction and contact forces.name: Friction State and Projection
mechanics::friction and contact forces.description: State judgment for rolling/slipping or friction projection along composite motion directions.
excludes: global work-energy audit without state judgment

rule_groups.name: Friction State Checks
rule_groups.summary: Checks friction-state identification and force projection under contact constraints.
rule_groups.activation_condition: Use when the key issue is whether friction is static/kinetic or how it projects onto motion.

mechanics::friction and contact forces.name: Contact Work and Constraint Consistency
mechanics::friction and contact forces.description: Contact problems where work, differential energy consistency, or anisotropic friction modeling are central.

rule_groups.name: Contact Work Checks
rule_groups.summary: Checks work and energy consistency in contact-force settings with nontrivial constraints or anisotropy.
rule_groups.activation_condition: Use when friction enters mainly through work or differential energy consistency.

mechanics::work-energy theorem and conse.name: Energy Baseline and Sign Consistency
mechanics::work-energy theorem and conse.description: Energy problems where baseline choice, sign convention, or redundant state variables determine correctness.
excludes: piecewise field stitching with geometry-specific transitions
orbital decay or celestial-orbit bookkeeping already covered by a dedicated gravitation cluster

rule_groups.name: Energy Baseline Checks
rule_groups.summary: Checks sign conventions, baseline alignment, and redundant-energy-state assumptions.
rule_groups.activation_condition: Use when the derivation can fail due to energy zero point, sign, or duplicated state information.

mechanics::work-energy theorem and conse.name: Constrained Path and Piecewise Energy Transfer
mechanics::work-energy theorem and conse.description: Energy transfer along constrained surfaces or piecewise force fields where kinetic stitching is required.
excludes: orbital decay or central-force orbit evolution already covered by a dedicated gravitation cluster

rule_groups.name: Path and Transfer Checks
rule_groups.summary: Checks kinetic-energy continuity and conservation along constrained paths or across segmented force regions.
rule_groups.activation_condition: Use when the energy flow is tied to path geometry or piecewise force regions.

mechanics::oscillations and simple harmo.name: SHM Parameterization and Phase
mechanics::oscillations and simple harmo.description: Single-oscillator SHM where phase, equilibrium position, or equation form is the central issue.

rule_groups.name: SHM Phase Checks
rule_groups.summary: Checks phase, equilibrium shift, and single-oscillator SHM parameter consistency.
rule_groups.activation_condition: Use when the task is about writing or interpreting the SHM equation itself.

mechanics::oscillations and simple harmo.name: Damping, Forcing, and Effective Modeling
mechanics::oscillations and simple harmo.description: Oscillation problems involving damping, forced-vs-free distinction, or equivalent stiffness/mass reduction.

rule_groups.name: Damping and Effective-Model Checks
rule_groups.summary: Checks damping law, forcing category, and equivalent reduction in oscillatory systems.
rule_groups.activation_condition: Use when the motion is not a clean undamped single oscillator and needs an effective model.

mechanics::oscillations and simple harmo.name: Mode Structure and Boundary Conditions
mechanics::oscillations and simple harmo.description: Oscillatory systems where mode identity, fixed-end phase behavior, or coupled frequency structure matters most.

rule_groups.name: Mode and Boundary Checks
rule_groups.summary: Checks whether oscillatory mode structure and end-condition reasoning are correctly identified.
rule_groups.activation_condition: Use when the problem turns on identifying a mode, standing pattern, or boundary-induced phase relation.

mechanics::normal modes and coupled osci.name: Mode Frequency and Period Structure
mechanics::normal modes and coupled osci.description: Coupled systems where the main check is mode period, frequency hierarchy, or collective oscillation structure.
excludes: derivation details of reduced coordinates only

rule_groups.name: Mode Period Checks
rule_groups.summary: Checks period and frequency structure in coupled oscillation systems.
rule_groups.activation_condition: Use when the key risk is misidentifying the collective period or mode frequency relation.

mechanics::normal modes and coupled osci.name: Boundary and Reduction Modeling
mechanics::normal modes and coupled osci.description: Coupled-mode setups that depend on boundary force treatment or reduced-coordinate derivation choices.

rule_groups.name: Boundary and Reduction Checks
rule_groups.summary: Checks whether coupled-mode derivations use the correct boundary force model and reduced-coordinate approximation.
rule_groups.activation_condition: Use when coupled-mode reasoning depends on derivation structure rather than direct frequency readout.

electromagnetism::current, resistance, a.name: Distributed Resistance and Geometry
electromagnetism::current, resistance, a.description: Resistance obtained from continuous geometry, spacing, or boundary-conditioned current paths.

rule_groups.name: Resistance Geometry Checks
rule_groups.summary: Checks whether geometric resistance construction uses the correct path length, spacing, and boundary assumptions.
rule_groups.activation_condition: Use when the main issue is building effective resistance from distributed geometry.

electromagnetism::current, resistance, a.name: Microscopic Transport and Decay Modeling
electromagnetism::current, resistance, a.description: Current problems governed by carrier-level parameters, microscopic transport, or nonstandard current decay models.

rule_groups.name: Transport and Decay Checks
rule_groups.summary: Checks microscopic transport relations and non-Ohmic decay-style current modeling.
rule_groups.activation_condition: Use when current behavior depends on carrier parameters or decay assumptions rather than static geometry.

electromagnetism::current, resistance, a.name: Ohmic Parameter and Circuit Identification
electromagnetism::current, resistance, a.description: Ohmic-law problems where the central task is identifying resistance, resistivity, or effective parameters from current-voltage relations in a DC-like setup.
excludes: inductive coupling as the dominant mechanism

rule_groups.name: Ohmic Identification Checks
rule_groups.summary: Checks whether static circuit parameters are inferred from the correct resistance and current-voltage relations.
rule_groups.activation_condition: Use when the main task is identifying a resistance-like parameter in a DC or quasi-static setup.

electromagnetism::self-inductance and mu.name: Coupled Inductors and Open-Circuit States
electromagnetism::self-inductance and mu.description: Problems where inductive coupling, branch connection state, or open-circuit behavior determines the correct voltage/current relation.

rule_groups.name: Coupled Inductor Checks
rule_groups.summary: Checks whether coupled-coil equations respect connection state and whether open branches are treated correctly.
rule_groups.activation_condition: Use when current or voltage depends on inductive coupling between multiple branches or coils.

electromagnetism::self-inductance and mu.name: Inductive Energy and Transient Response
electromagnetism::self-inductance and mu.description: Inductor-energy and transient problems where time evolution, L/R scales, or stored magnetic energy are the central audit path.

rule_groups.name: Inductive Transient Checks
rule_groups.summary: Checks whether inductive time response and stored-energy reasoning use the correct governing relation.
rule_groups.activation_condition: Use when the derivation depends on inductive transients, current decay, or magnetic-energy accounting.

electromagnetism::electric potential and.name: Potential Superposition and Reference Choice
electromagnetism::electric potential and.description: Electrostatic-potential problems where zero reference, superposition, or path-independent potential differences are central.
excludes: dipole far-field approximation as the main object

rule_groups.name: Potential Reference Checks
rule_groups.summary: Checks whether electrostatic potential is built with the correct reference, superposition, and path-independence assumptions.
rule_groups.activation_condition: Use when the derivation explicitly manipulates potential, potential difference, or electrostatic energy reference.

electromagnetism::electric potential and.name: Field-Potential Relation and Derivative Checks
electromagnetism::electric potential and.description: Problems where the electric field must be obtained from potential structure, gradients, or local derivative relations.

rule_groups.name: Field-Potential Checks
rule_groups.summary: Checks whether field quantities are derived from the correct potential relation and derivative structure.
rule_groups.activation_condition: Use when the solution differentiates or locally relates potential and field rather than only summing scalar potentials.

modern physics::relativistic energy and.name: Invariant and Threshold Kinematics
modern physics::relativistic energy and.description: Relativistic collision or decay problems where invariant mass, four-momentum, or threshold conditions provide the main audit path.

rule_groups.name: Invariant and Threshold Checks
rule_groups.summary: Checks relativistic collision and decay reasoning that depends on invariant mass or threshold conditions.
rule_groups.activation_condition: Use when the derivation centers on collision thresholds, invariant quantities, or four-momentum structure.

modern physics::relativistic energy and.name: Regime and Limit Checks
modern physics::relativistic energy and.description: Relativistic energy problems where the main audit path is distinguishing classical and relativistic regimes or using the correct limiting form.
excludes: threshold/invariant collision algebra as the main object

rule_groups.name: Relativistic Regime Checks
rule_groups.summary: Checks whether the solution uses the correct energy-momentum expression in the intended relativistic regime.
rule_groups.activation_condition: Use when the main risk is mixing classical and relativistic formulas or using the wrong limiting approximation.

thermodynamics & statistical physics::he.name: Mode Identification and Flux Balance
thermodynamics & statistical physics::he.description: Heat-transfer problems where the main task is identifying the dominant transport mode and writing the correct steady flux balance.

rule_groups.name: Heat Flux Mode Checks
rule_groups.summary: Checks whether the dominant heat-transfer mechanism and steady flux relations are chosen correctly.
rule_groups.activation_condition: Use when the derivation centers on transport mode identification or steady thermal flux balance.

thermodynamics & statistical physics::he.name: Heating, Cooling, and Capacity Models
thermodynamics & statistical physics::he.description: Thermal-evolution problems where heating/cooling, lumped heat capacity, or equilibrium approach is the main audit path.

rule_groups.name: Thermal Capacity Checks
rule_groups.summary: Checks whether transient heating/cooling and capacity-based thermal models are built correctly.
rule_groups.activation_condition: Use when the main risk is mis-modeling heat capacity, equilibrium, or heating/cooling time evolution.

thermodynamics & statistical physics::id.name: State Equation and Process Relations
thermodynamics & statistical physics::id.description: Gas problems where the main task is identifying the thermodynamic process and using the correct state relation.
excludes: heat-transfer transport mode as the main object

rule_groups.name: Gas Process Checks
rule_groups.summary: Checks whether gas-process classification and state relations are applied with the correct variables and constraints.
rule_groups.activation_condition: Use when the derivation depends on identifying or substituting the correct gas process relation.

thermodynamics & statistical physics::id.name: Gas Parameter and Model Boundary
thermodynamics & statistical physics::id.description: Problems where the key audit path is mapping gas parameters correctly and keeping ideal-gas assumptions separate from neighboring thermal models.

rule_groups.name: Gas Parameter Checks
rule_groups.summary: Checks parameter mapping and ideal-vs-neighbor-model boundaries in gas-state reasoning.
rule_groups.activation_condition: Use when the main risk is misidentifying gas parameters, degrees of freedom, or idealization boundaries.

thermodynamics & statistical physics::fi.name: Energy Bookkeeping and Sign Conventions
thermodynamics & statistical physics::fi.description: Thermodynamic problems where the main risk is misassigning heat/work signs or miswriting the first-law bookkeeping relation.
excludes: transport-mode-driven heat transfer as the main object

rule_groups.name: First-Law Sign Checks
rule_groups.summary: Checks whether the first law is written with the correct heat/work sign convention and energy bookkeeping.
rule_groups.activation_condition: Use when the derivation directly manipulates heat, work, and internal energy changes.

thermodynamics & statistical physics::fi.name: Closed-System Boundary and Process Scope
thermodynamics & statistical physics::fi.description: Thermodynamic bookkeeping problems where the main audit path is whether the chosen system boundary and process scope justify applying the first law in that form.
excludes: simple sign-only algebra with no boundary issue

rule_groups.name: First-Law Boundary Checks
rule_groups.summary: Checks whether the system boundary and process scope justify applying a closed-system first-law relation.
rule_groups.activation_condition: Use when the main risk is applying closed-system bookkeeping to an inappropriate process or boundary choice.

mechanics::circular motion and centripet.name: Centripetal Force and Speed Thresholds
mechanics::circular motion and centripet.description: Circular-motion problems where normal-force balance, centripetal acceleration, or critical speed is the main audit path.
excludes: Lorentz-force curvature when magnetic dynamics are primary

rule_groups.name: Centripetal Threshold Checks
rule_groups.summary: Checks whether circular-motion balance and threshold-speed conditions are set up with the correct force decomposition.
rule_groups.activation_condition: Use when the main risk is mis-writing the radial force balance or threshold speed condition.

mechanics::circular motion and centripet.name: Banked Contact and Constraint Geometry
mechanics::circular motion and centripet.description: Circular-motion setups where friction, banking, or geometric constraint decides whether contact forces can provide the needed centripetal effect.
excludes: pure free circular motion threshold only

rule_groups.name: Banked and Constraint Checks
rule_groups.summary: Checks whether banked or frictional circular-motion geometry is converted into the correct force balance.
rule_groups.activation_condition: Use when the centripetal effect comes from contact geometry or friction rather than a single explicit central force.

mechanics::rotational kinematics and dyn.name: Torque Balance and Angular Acceleration
mechanics::rotational kinematics and dyn.description: Rotational problems where torque balance and angular-acceleration equations are the primary route to the solution.

rule_groups.name: Torque Balance Checks
rule_groups.summary: Checks whether torque equations and angular-acceleration relations are written with the correct lever arm and sign.
rule_groups.activation_condition: Use when the solution depends on continuous torque balance rather than a one-shot conservation argument.

mechanics::rotational kinematics and dyn.name: Rolling and Rotation Constraints
mechanics::rotational kinematics and dyn.description: Rotational setups where rolling constraints, angular-linear coupling, or effective inertia relations are central.
excludes: pure torque-balance derivation with no kinematic constraint

rule_groups.name: Rolling Constraint Checks
rule_groups.summary: Checks whether rotational and translational variables are coupled with the correct rolling or inertia relation.
rule_groups.activation_condition: Use when the setup depends on no-slip constraints or mixed translational-rotational motion.

mechanics::angular momentum conservation.name: External Torque Validity
mechanics::angular momentum conservation.description: Angular-momentum conservation problems where the main check is whether external torque truly vanishes.
excludes: post-collision transfer details once validity is already clear

rule_groups.name: Angular Validity Checks
rule_groups.summary: Checks whether angular momentum conservation is invoked only after verifying that external torque is absent.
rule_groups.activation_condition: Use when the main risk is applying conservation in a system with hidden torque sources.

mechanics::angular momentum conservation.name: Collision and Reconfiguration Transfer
mechanics::angular momentum conservation.description: Problems where angular momentum is redistributed through collisions, shape change, or internal reconfiguration.
excludes: pure validity checking with no transfer step

rule_groups.name: Angular Transfer Checks
rule_groups.summary: Checks whether angular momentum is transferred and re-expressed correctly across collisions or changing inertia.
rule_groups.activation_condition: Use when the solution hinges on matching angular momentum before and after a collision or reconfiguration.

modern physics::cosmology and general re.name: Time Coordinates and Observer Effects
modern physics::cosmology and general re.description: GR or cosmology problems where proper time, coordinate time, or observer-dependent timing is the key distinction.

rule_groups.name: Time Coordinate Checks
rule_groups.summary: Checks whether relativistic timing uses the correct observer-dependent time variable and correction sign.
rule_groups.activation_condition: Use when the main risk is mixing proper time, coordinate time, or applied relativistic time corrections.

modern physics::cosmology and general re.name: Horizon and Cosmic Evolution
modern physics::cosmology and general re.description: Cosmology problems centered on horizons, FRW evolution, curvature terms, or dynamical-vs-boundary distinctions.

rule_groups.name: Cosmic Evolution Checks
rule_groups.summary: Checks horizon, expansion, and curvature-term reasoning in basic cosmology and GR settings.
rule_groups.activation_condition: Use when the statement is about large-scale evolution, horizon structure, or FRW-style dynamics.

mechanics::gravitation and kepler's laws.name: Orbital Decay and Orbit Accounting
mechanics::gravitation and kepler's laws.description: Satellite orbit change, orbital radius consistency, dissipative losses, and orbital-energy bookkeeping.

rule_groups.name: Orbit Decay Core Checks
rule_groups.summary: Checks whether orbital decay, radius, speed, and energy relations are modeled consistently.
rule_groups.activation_condition: Use when the problem centers on changing orbital radius, decay, circular orbit energy, or dissipative altitude loss.

mechanics::gravitation and kepler's laws.name: Binary and Multi-Body Reduction
mechanics::gravitation and kepler's laws.description: Two-body or multi-body systems that require reduced-mass or equivalent-single-body reasoning.

rule_groups.name: Binary Reduction Checks
rule_groups.summary: Checks whether binary or multi-body gravitational systems are reduced consistently before computation.
rule_groups.activation_condition: Use when the statement explicitly mentions two astronomical bodies orbiting or interacting as a system.

mechanics::gravitation and kepler's laws.name: Scattering and Deflection
mechanics::gravitation and kepler's laws.description: Flyby, deflection, and bending-angle reasoning, including distinctions between Newtonian and GR deflection treatments.
excludes: ordinary orbital decay and radius bookkeeping

rule_groups.name: Deflection Checks
rule_groups.summary: Checks whether scattering or bending-angle approximations are applied in the correct physical regime.
rule_groups.activation_condition: Use when the task is about a passing trajectory, bending angle, or relativistic correction to deflection.

mechanics::gravitation and kepler's laws.name: Escape and Visibility Geometry
mechanics::gravitation and kepler's laws.description: Escape conditions, elongation geometry, visibility time, and other orbital-geometry relations not tied to decay or scattering.

rule_groups.name: Geometry and Escape Checks
rule_groups.summary: Checks escape thresholds and celestial-geometry constraints in non-decay gravitational problems.
rule_groups.activation_condition: Use when the problem is about escape, visibility, elongation, or apsis geometry rather than dissipative orbit change.

modern physics::special relativity (time.name: Observation and Projection Geometry
modern physics::special relativity (time.description: Relativistic observation tasks where camera timing, geometric projection, or visible shape is central.
excludes: accelerated proper-time chains without observation geometry

rule_groups.name: Projection and Observation Checks
rule_groups.summary: Checks whether relativistic observation is treated as projection, simultaneous measurement, or another distinct observable.
rule_groups.activation_condition: Use when the problem asks what is seen, photographed, projected, or observed in a moving-frame geometry.

modern physics::special relativity (time.name: Accelerated and Non-Inertial Frames
modern physics::special relativity (time.description: Proper time, accelerated observers, rotating frames, and frame-coupling effects beyond simple inertial SR.

rule_groups.name: Non-Inertial Relativity Checks
rule_groups.summary: Checks proper-time relations and non-inertial frame corrections in accelerated or rotating relativistic settings.
rule_groups.activation_condition: Use when the statement includes acceleration, rotation, proper time, or equivalent frame-shift reasoning.

modern physics::special relativity (time.name: Wave, Frequency, and Reflection Effects
modern physics::special relativity (time.description: Relativistic Doppler, mirror reflection, threshold, or wave-frequency relations inside SR settings.
excludes: direct observation geometry without frequency transfer

rule_groups.name: Wave and Reflection Checks
rule_groups.summary: Checks whether relativistic wave relations are applied with the correct observable and frame conventions.
rule_groups.activation_condition: Use when the task centers on frequency, wavelength, mirror reflection, or threshold wave behavior.

modern physics::special relativity (time.name: Approximation and Metric Consistency
modern physics::special relativity (time.description: Metric relations, low-speed or high-order expansions, and consistency checks on relativistic approximations.
excludes: observation/photo geometry as the main object

rule_groups.name: Metric and Limit Checks
rule_groups.summary: Checks consistency of expansions, metric use, and limiting-form simplifications in SR derivations.
rule_groups.activation_condition: Use when the derivation explicitly relies on expansion, metric form, or approximation regime.

electromagnetism::electromagnetic induct.name: Motional EMF and Rotating Conductors
electromagnetism::electromagnetic induct.description: Moving or rotating conductors cutting field lines, including motional emf and phase conventions tied to rotation.

rule_groups.name: Motional and Rotation Checks
rule_groups.summary: Checks whether moving-conductor induction and rotating geometry are modeled with the correct emf source and sign convention.
rule_groups.activation_condition: Use when the source of emf comes from motion or rotation through a magnetic field.

electromagnetism::electromagnetic induct.name: Flux Integrals and Field Geometry
electromagnetism::electromagnetic induct.description: Problems dominated by magnetic flux construction, integration variables, and field geometry or average-field approximations.
excludes: explicit circuit transient focus without flux construction

rule_groups.name: Flux and Geometry Checks
rule_groups.summary: Checks whether induced emf is built from the correct flux variable, field geometry, and averaging assumptions.
rule_groups.activation_condition: Use when the main challenge is constructing or integrating magnetic flux through a geometry.

electromagnetism::electromagnetic induct.name: Induction Circuit Dynamics
electromagnetism::electromagnetic induct.description: Induction inside RL-like circuits, open/closed circuit states, induced-current interpretation, and current coupling logic.

rule_groups.name: Circuit Dynamics Checks
rule_groups.summary: Checks how induced emf, induced current, and circuit state are coupled in time-dependent induction problems.
rule_groups.activation_condition: Use when the statement focuses on circuit state, induced current evolution, or open/closed branch behavior.

electromagnetism::electromagnetic induct.name: Eddy Current and Force Balance
electromagnetism::electromagnetic induct.description: Eddy-current, induced-force, or power-balance problems where induction modifies motion or mechanical balance.
excludes: simple flux-only derivations with no mechanical consequence

rule_groups.name: Eddy Current and Force Checks
rule_groups.summary: Checks whether induction-driven forces, dissipation, and power balance are coupled consistently to motion.
rule_groups.activation_condition: Use when induced currents feed back into force balance, braking, or power exchange.

electromagnetism::dc circuits and kirchh.name: Loop and Node Equation Setup
electromagnetism::dc circuits and kirchh.description: Static circuit problems where the core issue is writing correct loop and node equations for branch currents and voltages.

rule_groups.name: Kirchhoff Setup Checks
rule_groups.summary: Checks whether loop and node equations are written with the correct sign, branch orientation, and unknown set.
rule_groups.activation_condition: Use when the solution depends on solving a static multi-branch circuit explicitly.

electromagnetism::dc circuits and kirchh.name: Equivalent Reduction and Loading
electromagnetism::dc circuits and kirchh.description: Circuit problems where equivalent resistance, source loading, or effective branch replacement is the main audit path.

rule_groups.name: Equivalent Reduction Checks
rule_groups.summary: Checks whether a static circuit is reduced or replaced using the correct effective-network logic.

electromagnetism::biot-savart law and am.name: Symmetry Loop and Field Direction

electromagnetism::biot-savart law and am.name: Biot-Savart Element Integration

electromagnetism::rl, rc, and rlc circui.name: Transient Response and Time Constants

rule_groups.summary: Checks whether reactive-circuit transients use the correct governing time constant and state transition logic.
rule_groups.activation_condition: Use when the solution depends on time evolution after switching or on exponential response behavior.

electromagnetism::rl, rc, and rlc circui.name: Resonance, Impedance, and Frequency Response
electromagnetism::rl, rc, and rlc circui.description: AC or oscillatory circuit problems where impedance composition, resonance, or frequency selection is the main route.
excludes: simple switch-on transient without frequency dependence

rule_groups.name: Resonance and Impedance Checks
rule_groups.summary: Checks whether reactive impedances and resonance conditions are combined with the correct frequency dependence.
rule_groups.activation_condition: Use when the main solution path is through impedance composition, resonance, or frequency-domain reasoning.

optics::snell's law and critical angle.name: Refractive Gradient and Mirage
optics::snell's law and critical angle.description: Continuously varying refractive index, mirage-like path bending, and critical-distance reasoning in stratified media.
excludes: optical-mechanical analogy used only as a secondary derivation trick

rule_groups.name: Gradient and Mirage Checks

optics::snell's law and critical angle.name: Optical-Mechanical Analogy
optics::snell's law and critical angle.description: Problems that recast path bending through effective velocity or potential analogies rather than direct Snell-law form.

rule_groups.name: Analogy-Based Checks
rule_groups.summary: Checks whether optical path reasoning is recast consistently through a mechanical analogy.
rule_groups.activation_condition: Use when the solution maps light-path bending to velocity, potential, or variational analogies.

optics::laser principles and application.name: Ring Resonator and Sagnac Devices
optics::laser principles and application.description: Ring-laser, fiber-loop, and Sagnac-type devices where path length, enclosed area, and opposite-direction propagation are central.

optics::laser principles and application.description: Laser cavity mode constraints, etalon filtering, and resonance-selection conditions.

optics::laser principles and application.name: Coherence and Source Behavior
